statement: For odd m, there are no positive integers u, B, C with 4uBC − u − B = m².
source: FRONTIER §1 T1 (ET Prop 1.6); METAPLECTIC_ES Thm K (D_t^-(tm²+1)=0)

statement: For every square n = m² and every u ≥ 1, n + u has no divisor d with d ≡ −1 (mod 4u).
For a prime p ≡ 1 (mod 4), u ≥ 1 and f | p + u with f ≡ −1 (mod 4u), f has a prime factor ℓ with (ℓ/p) = −1.
R(p) := #{(u,B,C) ∈ ℕ³ : 4uBC − u − B = p} is even for every odd prime p.
answer: true (divisor form counts d and its cofactor; FRONTIER §2.1)

statement: If n = 2^k divides z in a solution of 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z, then n divides x or y.
For p ≥ 5 prime and integers j ≠ j′ ≤ J, gcd(jp + 1, j′p + 1) divides j − j′.
source: FRONTIER §3 privacy of large primes (SS8 Lemma 2.3)

statement: For n ≥ 1 the graph on positive integers with an edge uv (u ≠ v) iff uv | n + u + v is a forest.
answer: true (each v > 1 has at most one smaller neighbour)

statement: Every positive solution of 4/n = 1/x+1/y+1/z with x ≤ y ≤ z satisfies x ≤ n, y ≤ 2n², z ≤ 2n⁴.
For odd n, 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + Q^k/Z with Q odd, gcd(Q, n) = gcd(Q, Z) = 1 is solvable for every odd k.
ES holds for every n = 3·2^s + 1, s ≥ 0.
M_BM(p) ≥ (3/(16π²) − o(1))(log p)² for primes p → ∞ (definition FRONTIER §2.2).
There are infinitely many primes p ≡ 1 (4) with R(p) ≥ (log p)^{100}.
8/131 is not a sum of three unit fractions.

For p = 3361, list all Type II solutions of 4/p.
List the primes p ≡ 1 (4), p ≤ 10⁹, with no word p = tuv − u − v (t,u,v ≥ 3) having a coordinate in 4ℤ ∪ (8ℤ − p).
Which odd non-squares n are exceptions to U(n) (as defined in the repo)?

statement: Find a prime p ≡ 1 (4), p > 10¹⁰, with R(p) = 0.
Prove the general-m Stickelberger identity of TWO_POWER_LADDER (known for m = 3, 4).
